notes: Human feedback for the MHM learning layer.
Use this for taste, placement and organization signals after reviewing the live map.
This file should stay factual and music-related. Do not add albums or songs as node targets.

feedbackCategories.label: Too dense
feedbackCategories.feedback: A local cluster is too compressed. Nodes may sit close together, but labels must remain readable and important names must not stack.

feedbackCategories.label: Label overlap
feedbackCategories.feedback: Visible labels collide or form unreadable piles. The renderer should hide lower-priority labels when zoomed out, and layout should increase spacing.

feedbackCategories.label: Wrong zone
feedbackCategories.feedback: A node is placed in a zone that does not match its strongest music-history context.

feedbackCategories.label: Good bridge
feedbackCategories.feedback: A node usefully connects two or more zones. Preserve its cross-zone pull instead of forcing it into a sealed cluster.

feedbackCategories.label: Bad node type
feedbackCategories.feedback: A candidate is not one of the allowed visible map node types: band, guitarist, artist, guitar, guitar_brand or genre.

feedbackCategories.label: Genre transition needed
feedbackCategories.feedback: Neighboring scenes need more documented bridge nodes so the map reads like a music-history flow, not separate boxes.

feedbackCategories.label: Category grouping
feedbackCategories.feedback: Category-like labels such as duos, groups, people, artists, albums or companies are not concrete music genres and should not become visible nodes.

feedbackCategories.label: Platform or reference
feedbackCategories.feedback: Music platforms, magazines, databases, institutions and reference works are source context, not visible map nodes.

bridgePolicies.feedback: The rock to hard-rock/metal path should overlap strongly. Let bridge nodes drift between zones rather than forming a straight, sterile lane.
Punk should connect back into rock history while keeping its own chaotic identity.
Hip-hop should keep a readable territory while allowing documented crossover lines into punk, rock and metal.

nodeFeedback.label: Misfits
nodeFeedback.feedback: Core punk and horror punk anchor. Keep near Ramones, Sex Pistols, horror punk and hardcore punk rather than generic rock.

nodeFeedback.label: Ramones
nodeFeedback.feedback: Major early punk anchor. Should help organize the punk-alt area and connect back to rock history.

nodeFeedback.label: Sex Pistols
nodeFeedback.feedback: Major UK punk anchor. Should sit in the punk-alt core with clear relation to Ramones and early punk.

nodeFeedback.label: Black Sabbath
nodeFeedback.feedback: Should behave as a bridge between hard rock, doom metal and heavy metal rather than sitting in a closed metal box.

nodeFeedback.label: Led Zeppelin
nodeFeedback.feedback: Important overlap point between blues rock, classic rock and hard rock.

nodeFeedback.label: Public Enemy
nodeFeedback.feedback: Hip-hop anchor with possible punk/rock crossover context. Keep hip-hop in its own area, but allow documented bridges.

zoneFeedback.feedback: Rock is the connective tissue. It should overlap with roots/blues, hard rock/metal, prog/psychedelia and punk instead of becoming a sealed box. Rock circuit may be dense and messy, but it must never become a crushed cluster. Nodes can sit close together, but labels should remain readable and should not overlap across multiple names. When rock, blues rock and hard rock nodes crowd together, spread them outward and preserve readable lanes between related groups.
Hard rock and metal should be dense, but not isolated. Black Sabbath, Led Zeppelin, Deep Purple, Van Halen, AC/DC and punk/metal crossover nodes should bleed across borders.
Punk/alternative should feel chaotic and connected, not boxed. Let hardcore, horror punk, post-punk and alternative scenes cluster, but allow cross-zone drift.
Hip-hop needs its own readable territory while still allowing documented crossover lines into funk, punk, rock and metal.

rules.feedback: Zones are guidance, not cages. Strong bridge nodes may bleed outside the visual rectangle when it improves readability.
Wikipedia categories are weak signals. Do not create or prioritize category-like genre nodes unless they are recognized music genres.
Songs, albums and releases can explain a connection, but should not become graph nodes.

Never allow the map to become visually unreadable. Dense clusters are acceptable when they feel like organized chaos, but labels must not overlap heavily, node labels must remain readable, and important names should not stack on top of each other. If a zone becomes too crowded, expand the local layout, increase spacing, or let bridge nodes drift outward instead of compressing everything into one tight cluster.
